I've been looking forward to seeing Sir Patrick Stewart return as Professor Charles Xavier in Avengers: Doomsday, especially knowing he'll be sharing the screen with Sir Ian McKellen again. The two actors have been part of the X-Men franchise for more than 25 years, and I can't imagine the flick without them. Although after Stewart's death in October, his final appearance will carry considerably more emotional weight than anyone originally anticipated. Now Marvel Studios president Kevin Feige and directors Joe and Anthony Russo are opening up about Stewart's last day on set for the upcoming Marvel movie, and I'm already getting emotional.

Speaking with Entertainment Weekly, Feige recalled a moment when the legendary actor addressed the crew after completing his work. Nobody knew for certain what it would mean at the time, but looking back, it sounds like Stewart knew he was saying goodbye. Marvel's head honcho revealed:

He stood up and he gave a speech to the crew. We didn’t know necessarily it would be his last day on a set, but he was sort of indicating to us that he thought it was.

Well, that got me. Stewart died at 86 on Oct. 29, making Doomsday his final on-screen performance. Knowing he apparently recognized the significance of that moment makes the story particularly heartbreaking.

I've always admired Stewart's ability to bring such extraordinary warmth and humanity to Charles Xavier. Even when the X-Men movies weren't particularly great, his presence could make a scene work. There's something incredibly moving about imagining the actor who spent decades portraying a mentor taking a moment to address the people who helped bring his final performance to life. Anthony Russo admitted that Stewart's farewell carried a weight that everyone seemed to recognize, even if nobody wanted to acknowledge what it might mean:

I think it was in the back of all of our heads, we may never see him on set again.

The director also revealed that Stewart was dealing with significant health challenges while filming. According to Russo, the actor's determination to deliver the performance was evident to everyone around him. And it wasn't easy watching someone they admired push himself so hard. He continued:

It was clear that he was struggling with his health, and he worked so hard to deliver a performance and a presence — for us as directors, for his other actors, for the crew. You could see it wasn’t just the effort of a regular actor showing up and delivering that kind of presence and performance and experience for others, collaboration. It was someone who was really being challenged in a very deep way on a health level, showing up and doing that. For him to have muscled through and delivered the performance that he did in that movie, and the experience that he delivered for all of us as collaborators, it made it intensely emotional.

I have a feeling that sentiment will carry over to audiences when the film finally arrives. Stewart first portrayed Xavier in the 2000s X-Men, eventually becoming one of the franchise's most recognizable faces. He returned for several sequels, delivered a particularly devastating performance in 2017's Logan, and later surprised MCU fans with an appearance in Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness.

Now, more than a quarter-century after his first appearance, he'll be returning alongside McKellen's Magneto. Joe Russo revealed that the longtime friends share an emotional scene about forgiveness, which could be especially difficult to watch under the circumstances.

Another detail from the interview makes this farewell even sadder. Stewart was reportedly offered a role in Avengers: Secret Wars as well, but chose to appear only in Doomsday. Feige also confirmed that Marvel is working on a tribute to the actor for the upcoming release.

I can't help thinking about how many people grew up with Stewart's Professor X, myself included. His portrayal helped define what new superhero movies could accomplish emotionally long before cinematic universes became the norm.

Knowing his final day involved such a heartfelt farewell to the people around him makes me appreciate his commitment even more. Whatever happens to Charles Xavier in Doomsday, I'm grateful Stewart got one last opportunity to play him.

Avengers: Doomsday arrives in theaters December 18 as part of the 2026 movie release schedule. I'll be bringing tissues.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

After two weeks of voting that bracketed the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6, Rockstar Games employees have voted overwhelmingly against a recognition agreement with the IWGB Game Workers Union.

25% of Rockstar employees voted in favor of the recognition agreement, the union said, while 75% voted against it. 1,544 employees took part in the vote, representing a turnout of just over 93%.

Rockstar workers actually founded a union earlier this year—the Rockstar Game Workers Union, a subsidiary of the Independent Workers Union of Great Britain—and it will continue to operate as it has. The IWGB said the outcome will not prevent Rockstar workers from organizing or exercising union rights, but the company will not be required to regularly meet with union representatives for collective bargaining or other relevant matters.

Despite the vote, the union said it will continue with organizing efforts at Rockstar.

"For anyone at Rockstar who believes in a fairer workplace, a fairer sector and a fairer society—this isn’t a sign to retreat, it’s a sign to double down on what we stand for. Hundreds of our coworkers voted in favour of our union at Rockstar, yet sadly we recognize we have more work to do to build understanding and win the trust of more of our colleagues," the IWGB Rockstar Game Workers Union said. "We’re ready to put in the effort to make that happen.

"Whilst we haven’t emerged with a recognition deal, this ballot has put our union on the radar of every worker, and opened the door for new kinds of conversation to start happening. People entirely unfamiliar with unions were for the first time debating employment conditions, collective bargaining rights, and our contracts. We heard from many more colleagues about what mattered to them, and we hope people will continue to engage so that we can see where these new discussions can lead us."

The power to shape our working lives has always been, and always will be, in our hands

In a separate statement, Rockstar head of publishing Jennfer Kolbe said the studio is "extraordinarily proud of our team, the culture we've built together and the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6."

From the creators of Edge: A free weekly videogame industry newsletter, featuring in-depth news, expert analysis and exclusive interviews

"This result reflects our team's strong support for continuing the direct relationships, collaboration and open dialogue that have helped make Rockstar Games so innovative and strong," Kolbe said. "As we look ahead, we're excited to build on all we've accomplished together."

Rockstar, which said it worked with the IWGB to ensure employees were able to make an informed decision in a fair and transparent vote, came under fire in October 2025 for firing more than 30 employees, all of whom were members of a private trade union Discord channel. The IWGB called it "the most ruthless act of union busting in the history of the UK games industry," while Rockstar says they were fired for leaking information about "upcoming and unannounced games." That matter is now before an employment tribunal; closing submissions were made last week.

#3634. With Grand Theft Auto 6, The Series Has Outgrown Some Of Its Joke Brand Names

One thing that keeps striking me about Grand Theft Auto 6 is how good the writing is, even compared to that in previous games in the series. I enjoyed those earlier games, sure, but the dialogue and storytelling in GTA 6 are a cut above the rest in terms of both the game’s compelling characters and its worldbuilding. The fact that GTAÂ is set in an analogue of the real world helps the worldbuilding bridge gaps that most fictional universes couldnât, but Iâm increasingly finding that the standout writing is fighting a war within the game itself against some of the other jokes that have been building up in the series for over a quarter century.

Grand Theft Auto, for obvious reasons, canât use the existing brand names that we see every day in real life. In this sense it’s the opposite of the Like a Dragon series, which proudly wears all its licensed brand deals on its chest and even had to write a narrative around losing the license to a key landmark in the seventh game in the series. Talking Budweiser into lending their brand name to GTA 4 would have been an uphill battle and maybe also raised some uncomfortable questions about the gameâs proximity to real-world places and events. Better to just call your in-game equivalent Pisswasser and move on.

But weâre in 2026 now. The writing in theÂ GTA games has elevated and, to Rockstarâs credit, so have the fake brand names in general. Taco Bomb is a pretty good one as a stand-in for Taco Bell. ZIP for GAP is also good. Weazel News for Fox News makes sense on a couple of different levels, Snapmatic for Instagram is something that you recognize immediately upon hearing it. But there are a handful of brand names I think the series needs to ditch, as theyâre taking away from the more interesting narratives Rockstar wants to tell.

Pisswasser is not a bad joke on its own, but it wears its welcome out fast. Marbles, the McDonaldâs stand-in in GTA, sells a burger called Big Balls. I get it, Big Mac, Big Balls, sure. But come on, man. Weâre scraping the bottom of the barrel here. Zombix isnât even a good pun. Itâs like someone filed that one in the ten minutes before the deadline. We need to start thinking intelligently about which of these benefit worldbuilding and which detract from it.

I’m not saying all of these need to go or even a majority of them. There are plenty of good joke brand names, but there are also ones that are very, very 2000s, and it would be better for the games if they disappear. Grand Theft Auto has grown with its audience, and it’s now delivering narratives that genuinely keep up with well-written modern movies, so why are we limiting aspects of it to jokes that would appear in an Epic Movie parody?

Rockstar can and should start taking a look at these and see what makes sense for their games every so often. Audit the world, donât just assume that because it existed in previous games, it needs to exist forever.

Itâs not like brands donât just disappear from the real world all the time. Joannâs Fabrics isnât around anymore, but your world keeps spinning, just like it would if the Obey car line simply did not appear in a new game. You planning to take a Spirit Airlines flight this holiday? Youâre sure as hell not, nor would you be a sobbing mess on the floor if a Big Balls sandwich billboard wasnât overlooking a highway chase.

There are already so many good jokes in these games that the lame ones can get cut out without losing anything. No one is wrong for liking them, but maybe the games themselves can be better for examining what works and what doesnât. No series has ever escaped a need for refreshing itself and iterating over the years and, in almost every way, GTA 6 nails it. Thereâs just one more thing I want to see them look at before they build their next GTA world, asking themselves if each jokey brand name still fits their vision. If it does, great! If they decide it would be better to snip, that would be fine, too.

#3633. After playing the game, 30% of polled GTA 6 players want to buy flowers for a loved one, 9% accidentally punched cats

A new survey of Grand Theft Auto 6 players has found some particularly interesting results. 30 percent came away from the game with the desire to buy someone special flowers. Nine percent punched cats.

Per Games User Research's director Steve Bromley, 303 players from across the UK and US were polled on their experiences. They had to have at least two hours of playtime to contribute, which led to an informed sample of how folks are finding the game.

Those polled gave the game an 8.4/10 (that's 4.2/5 Eurogamer readers), which is glowing praise. 42 percent loved the narrative, as well as Jason and Lucia's relationship. 38 dug the lifelike and believable world, while 35 percent were keen on the freedom to explore and the variety of activities.

As for what they didn't like, 28 percent weren't a fan of the slow pacing and long cutscenes, 19 percent didn't like the difficulty in stealing cars and losing a wanted level, while 18 percent were put off by the game's technical performance.

Now for some fun findings: 41 percent expressed an interest in improving their real life after playing the game, with 30 percent of those looking to buy a loved one some flowers. Nice! 14 percent were at least once confused or stuck, due to confusion with the stealth, identifying time-sensitive missions, or experiencing control issues.

There's some bad news for the cats out there, too. Nine percent accidentally punched a cat while trying to pet it, while 61 percent had the same experience with human NPCs. At least it wasn't intentional, that has to count for something. Right?

Taylor Swift has been dealing with a lot this week. Of course, there’s the expose about her that led to comments about Ugg boots and more going viral. Now, a lawsuit she’s involved in has come back into the spotlight, as she’s asking a judge to intervene in it.

Earlier this year, Maren Flagg, who performs under the name Maren Wade, filed a trademark lawsuit against Taylor Swift. She claimed she trademarked “Confessions of a Showgirl” in 2015, and she was of the opinion that Swift’s album, The Life of a Showgirl, impacted her brand. She also said (via Variety) that the album and her brand “share the same structure, the same dominant phrase, and the same overall commercial impression.” She asked for an injunction to stop Swift from using The Life of a Showgirl brand.

In response, Swift’s lawyers called this argument “absurd.” Now, according to a new report from TMZ, the singer is asking a judge to intervene in all of this. New documents showed that the pop star did not approve of Flagg’s latest efforts to have their legal battle in California, as her motion read:

Wade is arguing that she can sue the singer in California because she performs there. Swift did perform at the Academy Museum Gala in LA recently. However, according to the pop star’s team, a performance in the state does not mean she can be sued there, and she doesn’t have a legal connection to California.

Now, as this is all unfolding, Taylor Swift is also at the center of many other stories. Most controversially, the Vanity Fair expose about her is making waves. It did not paint Swift in a good light; however, it’s also being met with a lot of backlash.

There’s also the whole issue with the shrubs and security Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce are working to implement around their home in Ohio. Those were ultimately approved; however, many people who live in that neighborhood were not happy about it.

However, there are good things going on too. Just last week, Swift performed at the CMA Awards, and she’s been on the Oscar campaign trail for her Toy Story 5 song. She released encore songs for The Life of a Showgirl this fall, too, and as always, the theorizing about when we might see Taylor Swift (Taylor’s Version) and/or her 13th album is ongoing.

Oh, and she’s been spotted in the stands cheering on her husband, Travis Kelce, at his games. Speaking of Kelce and Swift, they had the wedding of the year this summer at Madison Square Garden. And those who went seemingly have nothing but the best things to say about the “intimate” event.

All this is to say, Taylor Swift has been taking the good with the bad, and that’s been happening throughout her career. Now, as we learn more about this lawsuit that seems to have a new wrinkle, we’ll keep you posted.

#3630. We are already in a world where people think about promoting games as human-made, Citizen Sleeper creator says

Citizen Sleeper creator Gareth Damian Martin - also known by their studio name Jump Over the Age - believes we're reaching a point of gen-AI saturation whereby game-makers are starting to counter-promote games as being human-made.

"We already are. Yeah, yeah, yeah. 100 percent," Damian Martin told me in an interview, while discussing their striking new game Signet City. "That was already something that my publisher [Fellow Traveller] was saying they want to do with my games more, especially with me doing the art this time as well. Yeah, 100 percent - it's going to give rise to that."

It's a label I haven't seen circulating in games yet, but we have seen an increase in the number of AI disclosures for games being sold on Steam, and many videos on YouTube now carry 'No AI' badges, in an effort to stand out from the torrent of videos made using gen-AI. We are already seeing Steam events dedicated to games without any AI usage whatsoever. Things are clearly changing.

Damian Martin told me "the only good thing" that could come from gen-AI use is a bounce-back effect of people noticing and cherishing human-made things more. They were reminded of this while looking at a Rembrandt sketch while doing a brief stint in art school ahead of Signet City (the art in the Citizen Sleeper games was commissioned, but the art in Signet City is done by them). In the sketch, the faces had been scribbled out, presumably because Rembrandt didn't like the work he'd done. They were scribbles that revealed the humanity of the creator.

"You suddenly remember that trying to represent a human face by using a pencil and a piece of paper is something that's been happening for hundreds of years," Damian Martin said. "So when you do it, you're connecting to an entire history of that challenge and that opportunity, and it's fascinating to me to engage and be part of that. It's really beautiful.

"If AI makes us notice that more," they added, "then I think that's great. If we can make a counter-punch, if we can find that energy, that's great. I certainly think if it gives value to human-made things, in a way that perhaps we'd been forgetting, then that's the only good thing that can come from that process."

To be clear, Damian Martin is not using gen-AI in making Signet City, a game about being a parasite in people's heads in a fictional version of Newcastle in the 1980s and then influencing what they do. It's a game with a distinct hand-drawn look, presented in a thick-lined, moody black-and-white way, and with bleak industrial backgrounds and post-punk influences and energy. Indeed, the idea Damian Martin would use gen-AI in any way runs counter and contrary to what they're known for.

"I exist in this space where the idea that I would use AI is kind of mad," they said. "It's a bit like me saying, 'I'm going to start buying all of my art materials from the asset store on Unity.' The reason people buy my games is because they come from me, and the only evidence I have - the only thing I can trust - is my own expression and identity. That's the thing that's worked for me; there's no other judgeable thing. So I'm working to put more of that into my games.

"But there is a real threat," they added, "and the reason there is a real threat in the wider games industry is because it's an industry, and people who work on games for big companies, in my experience, are treated very poorly. They are not respected as human beings in a lot of cases. So why would they not be replaced by machines if the people who pay their wages do not even respect their human nature? They do not respect their creativity. We've seen such a lack of respect for expression, for directors, for individuals within games."

"When something is industrial production and it doesn't care about the people involved, then it doesn't care whether they're machines or they're people as long as the work happens, and that's the real threat," they reiterated. "So we do have to be vigilant, and we do have to be loud and say stuff, and say that it's not okay for us, because otherwise it will happen. It just seems inevitable that you would try to automate these things because it's easier than having employees; that's the kind of horrible logic of industry, unfortunately. But that doesn't really concern me because I'm operating in a completely different mode."

Signet City currently has no release date but was said to be halfway through development when announced this summer. Citizen Sleeper 2 - Damian Martin's most recent game - was released at the beginning of 2025. It's a sequel that introduced more pressure into the heartwarming sci-fi, dice-rolling, role-playing series, and I thought it better for it. "With a new found sense of tension, and showpiece Contract missions, Citizen Sleeper is transformed. This follow-up has improved the RPG formula in every way," I wrote in my Citizen Sleeper 2 review.

Grand Theft Auto 6 might feel more grounded compared to its predecessors, but that doesn't mean Leonida isn't full of weird and supernatural ongoings. One such paranormal activity is GTA 6's aliens—if you know where to look, you'll be able to find a UFO which'll eventually lead you down a strange road of cows, radiation, and the aliens themselves.

And if you don't know where to look, here's where I can help you. If you want to find GTA 6's UFO and a weird little alien guy, here's exactly where you need to go and what you need to do.

The alien abduction is actually a three-parter mission, and to get started you'll first need to locate the abandoned car. You'll need to look for it at nighttime, and it can spawn in a number of locations. For me, it was a little ways east of Port Gellhorn in Kelly County. For our own Chris Livingston, he discovered the car somewhere north of Capri, also in Kelly County. You know it's the one if the car is pointed toward a forest and the doors are open.

Once you've found it, you'll need to follow the path it's parked along. You'll know you're going the right way by the clothes strewn along the path. If it's a bit too dark or you're stuck, you can press L3 + R3 to activate your focus and see the clothes more easily or equip your flashlight. Eventually you'll see the lights of the UFO and a very naked lady amongst it all. Head over until a cutscene plays out.

Once that's over, you'll get into a light scuffle with the woman before she instructs you to go get her car. Head back to where you first found the vehicle, where one more cutscene will play out and you'll be done… for now.

You'll need to wait for some time to pass. Make sure you're heading home and going to sleep each night, preferably as whichever character you discovered the UFO on. Eventually, you'll trigger a cutscene that'll bring you to a white room.

Find the dark oval which signals the way to a corridor and run through it. You'll be met with a terrifying maze of eggs. Get close to them and they'll start glowing blue. Get too close and they'll turn yellow, eventually cracking and causing your character to be yoinked back to the start by tentacles.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

Carefully make your way through the eggs, finding large gaps where you won't cause them to break. Once you've made it to the other side, you'll be met with another room containing the solar system. Take a look at earth—this is actually showing you where you'll need to head for part three of this mission—and continue onwards until you reach a code.

To decipher the code, simply look at how many lines are in each of the four symbols above the keypad. For me, the code was 3124. Punch in the code, and head to the next room.

Here, you'll need to push the button on the control panel and light it up. The aim is to have four green lights, so keep pushing until all four are the same colour and then pull the lever to the left.

Once that's done, you'll be met with three metal doors. The middle one'll do some nasty damage if you step into the room and hang around too long, so avoid it. Instead, head to the room on the left—yes, the one with the cows—and run in to grab the bottle of milk on the table.

Run back out and head for the door on the right. Walk to the end until you see a contraption where you're able to insert your milk bottle. Shortly after, you'll wake up back in your bed and ready to tackle the final part of this mission chain.

You'll want to head over to the location shown to you in the globe. More specifically, you'll want to head south of Hamlet, at this abandoned building just west of the river.

There'll be a gap in the fence you can hop over, or you can shoot the padlock, or alternatively ram into the gate with your car. From here, you can either climb on top of the roof and drop down or find the double doors and kick them down, or use the snap gun. Either way, you'll want to make sure the door is unlocked for later in this mission.

Turn around and head down the stairs, towards the keypad at the end of the corridor. The code here is the same as the one you used earlier, so punch it in again and head into the elevator.

Walk through the tunnel and you'll once again be met with a control panel and three doors, plus a little audiotape with some fun exposition about alien experimentation. You'll be doing the exact same thing here as you did earlier—get every light to green, push the lever, and head into the left room to retrieve a bottle of milk. The middle room once again doles out gnarly damage, so don't hang too long or avoid it all together.

Head over to the door on the right, down the corridor and into the room. Insert the milk bottle into the contraption and after a few seconds, out will pop a little alien guy! It's unconscious, though, so you'll need to pick it up.

As soon as you've picked up the alien, the bunker will begin to fill with toxic gas and you'll need to head out ASAP. Go back the way you came—through the tunnel and into the elevator, and then through those double doors you snap gunned/kicked down earlier to get outside.

Sadly, your time with this alien fella is brief, as it'll quickly get beamed up into the sky by a UFO. It also doesn't take long for special forces to show up, but don't worry. The UFO will return to laser them all down, allowing you to get out without any further issues.

For your troubles, the aliens will give you a permanent buff to your health, stamina, and focus, so helping out these extraterrestrials is more than worth the effort. And, y'know, the trauma.

#3627. Rockstar Games employees vote against union recognition

Rockstar Games employees have voted against official recognition of the Rockstar Game Workers Union, with 93.2 percent of staff participating in the vote.

25 percent of those who participated voted to recognise the union, while 75 percent voted against. If it had been approved, it would have been the largest recognised union in the UK video game industry by a large margin. While the union will still exist and organise, Rockstar Games will not have to recognise the union as a representing body for staff at the studio, and is not obligated to attend regular meetings with the body.

Jennifer Kolbe, head of publishing at Rockstar Games told Eurogamer: "We are extraordinarily proud of our team, the culture we've built together and the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6. This result reflects our team's strong support for continuing the direct relationships, collaboration and open dialogue that have helped make Rockstar Games so innovative and strong. As we look ahead, we're excited to build on all we've accomplished together."

The Rockstar Union also released a statement following the outcome of this vote, saying Rockstar employees will continue to organise despite the lack of recognition. It reads:

"For anyone at Rockstar who believes in a fairer workplace, a fairer sector and a fairer society - this isn't a sign to retreat, it's a sign to double down on what we stand for. Hundreds of our coworkers voted in favour of our union at Rockstar, yet sadly we recognise we have more work to do to build understanding and win the trust of more of our colleagues. We're ready to put in the effort to make that happen.

"Whilst we haven't emerged with a recognition deal, this ballot has put our union on the radar of every worker, and opened the door for new kinds of conversation to start happening. People entirely unfamiliar with unions were for the first time debating employment conditions, collective bargaining rights, and our contracts. We heard from many more colleagues about what mattered to them, and we hope people will continue to engage so that we can see where these new discussions can lead us.

"A recognition agreement would have marked a path towards greater workplace democracy. But it's one route of many. At Rockstar we have already won, and will continue to win, tangible changes that improve our everyday lives. We'll keep fighting for a say. For pay transparency, contractual overtime pay, and protections against Al and layoffs.

"The power to shape our working lives has always been, and will always be, in our hands."

Rockstar employees represented by the union are still awaiting the verdict from the Rockstar Games vs IWGB employment tribunal legal case, of which the final verdict is still pending. This case was kicked off by the sudden firing of employees present in a union Discord server. The employees claim this was an attempt at union busting by Rockstar, while the company denies this, saying it was for breaking confidentiality agreements.

WWE moved away from Survivor Series’ traditional format of all multi-man matches in the mid 90s. I get where Vince McMahon and company were coming from. It’s harder to build when you have so many moving parts, and it was harder to get people to buy PPVs back in the day without world title matches. In an effort to get back to the spirit of Survivor Series, Triple H has used a men’s and women’s WarGames match the last few years to keep that 5 on 5 format, but the event doesn't have quite the same prestige it once did. This year, however, he also threw in an old school Survivor Series elimination match, and the build has been the best thing on WWE television in months.

Seriously, if you have not been watching the segments for the United States versus Mexico match over the past several weeks, you have missed out big time. Cody Rhodes was picked as captain of the United States team. He quickly added CM Punk, who promptly appointed himself as co-captain. Since then, they’ve been trying to fill out the roster, and it’s led to a nice showcase for team members LA Knight and Je’Von Evans, as well as a fun segment with proposed team member The Miz and maybe the best segment of the entire year with a 70-something year old Hacksaw Jim Duggan who joined the team and then promptly quit after seeing a highlight reel of their Mexican opponents. I cannot freaking wait for the match, especially after Seth Rollins was added to maximize the drama.

Fortunately, there are some other exciting matches to look forward to, as well. The men’s War Games will feature the Bloodline against the 946, the latter of whom feel like they’re building some real momentum and are an actual threat to win. The women’s War Games match hasn’t had quite the same build, but it still features some top talent and should be a good showcase for younger talent as well. Throw in a pretty compelling Women’s World Championship match with Liv Morgan and Becky Lynch, and the card is really pretty solid.

Before I get into what I think is going to happen in each match, you can check out how I’ve done on predictions. I’ve given my take ahead of every PLE since WrestleMania 38, and while I’m not going to main event WrestleMania with this win-loss record, I could be competing for a midcard championship. Here’s a quick snapshot of the bigger WWE PLEs this year, as well as the overall record…

With all due respect to Team Mexico and especially Penta who currently holds the Money In The Bank Briefcase, this match is lopsided on paper. Cody, CM Punk and Seth are three of the biggest stars in the entire company, and Rhdoes especially does not lose unless it’s in a very key spot or in service of building to something larger or very memorably at WrestleMania 39, both. This match, however, feels like it’s really building toward something larger. It feels like a Mega Powers explode situation.

There’s been so much talk about Cody Rhodes possibly turning heel after punting Randy Orton, but I think it’s more likely we’re going to see CM Punk turn on Cody, or potentially turn full heel, as he’s clearly irate about Rhodes adding his longtime enemy Seth Rollins to the team. At minimum, the story of this match is going to be about the simmering tension between Rhodes, Punk and Rollins. Now, does that mean they’re going to actually lose the match? Not necessarily.

They could fight amongst themselves and wind up with some shock eliminations, or they could fight through the tension and win, pushing the inevitable turn further down the road.

I feel like the long-term goal here is to move us into a feud with Liv Morgan and Roxanne Perez. Rumors have swirled that Perez was originally slated to win Money In The Bank. She appeared in Morgan’s backstage segment with her this past Monday. Lynch has talked about how Judgment Day is holding her back. She’s clearly going to play a factor here in some way. It would be easy to say she’ll turn on Morgan and cost her the belt, but I don’t think that’s going to happen.

First, I don’t think there’s been enough teasing of a Judgment Day break-up. Fans have speculated about it forever, but we haven’t gotten nearly enough friction since Finn left to maximize the possible payoff here. Doing it now would be underbaked and stupid. Second, I think what Roxanne actually wants is a shot at the title, and she’s going to ruin that if Morgan loses the title. So, I think she’s going to help her ensure Liv keeps it.

Throw in the fact that Liv is already committed to the John Cena classic, and I feel pretty confident she’s going to hold onto the belt here.

For the longest time, I was sure we were headed toward an Alexa Bliss and Charlotte Flair break-up, but curiously, WWE really hasn’t teased much friction between the two lately, not since Tatum Paxley's early main roster promotion. Without that dynamic, this really just feels like a run of the mill babyfaces vs heels match that we would get at a house show.

Maybe there’s an angle I’m not seeing here or one that will emerge during the show, but absent that, I’m going to pick the babyfaces because when in doubt, always pick the babyfaces. That’s just a standard wrestling rule, and given I think there’s a potential for a lot of heels to win on this card, it makes even more sense to go with the babyfaces.

Predicted Winner: Charlotte Flair, Alexa Bliss, Tatum Paxley, Stephanie Vaquer and Bayley.

This is the moment where we find out how WWE really feels about 946 and Royce Keys. They’ve been the primary antagonists on the show for months and have been presented like really dangerous and unhinged monsters we should take seriously. If they lose here, it kind of feels like that’s the end. I mean I’m not saying they’re going to get released, but it feels like that’s the end of the audience taking them seriously. They’re the ones stepping up and trying to prove they’re main event players. If they lose in their first big PLE match trying to do that, then that tells the audience all they need to know.

I think WWE believes in them more than that. I think they also believe in the recently added Cruz Montana, and I think they see the 946 as another chance to push Carmelo. They really need this win in a way the Bloodline doesn’t, and if they do win, it would make all the sense in the world to build toward Keys getting a legit title shot at Royal Rumble against Roman Reigns. He would be a big underdog in that match, but he would at least be coming off some momentum from a victory here.

I think the 946 really needs to win, but WWE also almost never has the Bloodline actually lose. So, do I feel confident about this? No.

#3625. GTA 6 reportedly sets massive livestreaming record, watched more in its first week than Elden Ring, Diablo 4, Valorant, and Lost Ark combined

Grand Theft Auto 6 has broken another livestreaming record. After attracting more viewers across livestreaming platforms than any game ever on its launch day, Rockstar's open-world crime sim has reportedly continued to dominate on platforms like Twitch, YouTube, and Kick.

Over its first seven days on sale, GTA 6 has amassed over 420m hours watched, according to Streams Charts. That's nearly three times more than the previous record, held by Valorant's closed beta in April 2020. In fact, that 420m hours tally is more than the first-week watch time achieved by Valorant, Elden Ring, Diablo 4, and Lost Ark combined.

As for the livestreaming platforms that saw the largest audiences for GTA 6, YouTube reportedly had the lead in average audience numbers during the first six hours of launch, but Twitch took over in content volume in the days that followed. In fact, Twitch's GTA 6 watch time was higher at launch than any other game in its history.

Streams Charts also noted 1,056 channels reached new all-time peak viewership numbers while streaming GTA 6, in some cases multiplying their previous record tenfold. Major content creators like IShowSpeed, IlloJuan, and TheBurntPeanut stole the spotlight, but GTA 6 also helped many other channels set new viewership records.

Livestreaming, of course, isn't the only area where GTA 6 has set new records. Publisher Take-Two called it the biggest entertainment launch in history, generating $3.79bn (£2.89bn) in revenue from 32.5m copies sold on day one. Other parts of the industry have benefited, too. Anticipation for GTA 6 boosted US hardware sales for both PlayStation and Xbox, just as GTA 6 became each console brand's most pre-ordered title ever. At launch, more than 39 million people played GTA 6 on PS5, according to Sony. The game also had the highest number of concurrent players ever on any PlayStation console, beating even the most popular free-to-play titles.

You can check out Eurogamer's GTA 6 walkthrough if you're in need of assistance, which we just updated today with a guide on how to whistle in GTA 6 - something I didn't know you could do. The walkthrough also covers other lesser-known mechanics such as how to steal ATMs in GTA 6, and much more besides.

Grand Theft Auto 6 doesn't just mark a huge, and at times unbelievable, step forward for graphics; it's also at the forefront of what an open world game can be, just look at the existential crisis it's given Cyberpunk 2's creative director. With thousands of enterable buildings, unpredictable and slightly scary NPCs, and systems that help you determine what kind of criminal you want to be. It all really does feel like a milestone for what videogames can do.

"As the resolution goes up, you want the sophistication of the experience to go up, and obviously the sophistication of the mechanics," Rob Nelson, Rockstar's head of development, says in an interview with Eurogamer. "So it just naturally flowed that we give players choices to interact with the world beyond just violence, beyond just 'down the barrel of a gun', because it's fun."

The sophisticated mechanics that Nelson is talking about here pertains to GTA 6's Criminal Profile, a system that evaluates your escapades across Leonida and gives you a rating. There's Professional, Hardened, Violent, Psycho, and Irredeemable. The more stealthy and non-lethal you are, the higher your profile will be. It's similar to Red Dead Redemption 2's Honor System.

"There was maybe more emotional resonance in the story of RDR2 than we had, certainly in a GTA before," Nelson says. "So we liked that idea. We didn't necessarily come to GTA 6 going: 'We must have emotional resonance,' but all of those things combine. It's more that those systems and that element of player choice and agency, and the way that affected the narrative, was a hard thing to ignore and walk away from."

Nelson explains that most of the groundwork started as "simple things" in principle, "but they create a lot more work in terms of development of the sophistication of the systems." It's all about choice in GTA 6. You choose whether you want to be a criminal with a conscience or a loose cannon.

"It's still a world of violence, but you could threaten somebody by aiming a gun at them and just robbing them, and they have a chance to comply. So you don't have to beat them to death to get their money."

The part that sticks out the most is that you "don't have to" approach crimes in a certain way, there's still the option to go into every encounter guns blazing because redemption only works from a storytelling perspective when it's the player's choice, and not as Nelson puts it, something that is "foisted upon you".

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

"You can still go on those rampages and basically smash your Criminal Profile until it breaks," Nelson adds. "And then you enter this irredeemable state, which basically says, 'I reject your criminal profile system! I don't want it.'"

Am I brave enough to reject the criminal profile system entirely? Hell no. I replay sections of dialogue if I accidentally upset someone, and cannot do an "evil run" of a game without giving myself stomach ulcers because of the guilt—but I appreciate having the option.

#3622. "Where's the ding?!!" - I asked the PowerWash Simulator 2 team what they thought of Jason's nozzle work in GTA 6

Among the many, many side activities you can do in GTA 6, there's powerwashing. Relatively early on, as part of Chapter 1's Down to Earth mission, Jason whips out his nozzle and blasts Brian's boat to a gleaming sheen. Disappointingly for powerwashing fans, though, it's a bit of a one-and-done gag, never to return. But powerwashing is powerwashing, and we immediately wondered what the experts made of it all. Had Rockstar, with its legendary attention to detail, accurately captured the intricacies of powerwashing in those leisurely moments of carefree squirting?

A question had been asked and an answer was required. So who better to cast judgement on the authenticity of Jason's sway-and-spraying than FuturLab, the studio behind the delightfully zen PowerWash Simulator series? Thus, in a moment of whimsy, I asked if it might like to 'review' GTA 6's hosiest activity. At best, I was hoping for a cheeky little statement; I certainly wasn't expecting a big chunk of the PowerWash Simulator 2 team to join in the fun. "Fair to say," the intermediary PR noted, "the Futurlab team was excited about this one!"

So what's the verdict? Let us turn to the pros. "They've got the sounds and satisfaction of clearly a nice shiny flat surface just right," PowerWash Simulator 2 lead game designer Nick McCarthy opined, "but where's the ding!? 0/10, needs 200 percent more layers of muck and 20 percent more parkour." And quickly a trend emerged. "Great visuals, satisfying feel, but lacks the crucial ding and went by too quickly to listen to a podcast," senior programmer Will Dyball wrote. Then still more sadness for the lack of PowerWash Simulator's most motivating sound: "Didn't hear a ding," associate publishing producer Jess Crosby wrote. "Must have missed a bit."

A few team members also spotted some powerwashing faux pas. "No soap?" wrote 3D artist Eilidh Norris. "Rookie mistake, Jason." Programmer Jordan Lewis also reckoned Jason was making things unnecessarily hard for himself: "[He'd] have had an easier time had he taken the time to upgrade his washer and purchased some more nozzles," they wrote. "PS. Soap would have gotten that off in a flash." Others had safety concerns: "I find Jason's lack of protective overalls disturbing," said 3D artist Rory Peace, and data principal Russell Young agreed. "Clean speedboat, ruined clothes. Don't want to bring them 'Down to Earth', but we need to talk about PPE." People advisor Sarah Robshaw, meanwhile, spotted a more heinous omission: "Where's the cats????"

Elsewhere, game designer Sam Jenkins was delighted by the powerwashing representation. "I'm so glad that the Art of Powerwashing is being taken more seriously in mainstream games!" they wrote. "However, I think the dirt on the boat is too scarce for that satisfying cleaning contrast to come through."

Jenkins even had some expert suggestions to make Jason's little squirt-out more rewarding: "Maybe the boat should have been left in a flooded warehouse for 30 years to coat it in grime?" they continued. "Or even have a crushed fruit festival come through town to get some nice big colourful blobs all over the boat. Ooh! And we could even have the boat be the home of various squids to get some difficult-to-clean Ink streaked down it too!" Truly the words of someone who takes their powerwashing seriously!

Junior build engineer Owen Layton, programmer Jordan Lewis, and lead designer Nick McCarthy also provided 'reviews' in pictoral form, but technical complications mean they'll just have to exist in your imagination. Senior narrative designer Mark Ginbey, though, expressed admiration for all the in-world encouragement players are given. "Some excellent motivational text updates from Cal, like 'Mmhmm, half way there...' to indicate 50 percent completion," they wrote. "But Jason needs to concentrate on the work in hand. A quality powerwasher never talks on the job."

Senior game designer António Salreta had praise for GTA 6, with one exception: "It's an amazing game with so many fun systems - but. Needs. More. Nozzles." And how's this for a ringing endorsement from senior QA tester Paul Comse? "I love coming home after a hard day of work powerwashing in PowerWash Sim and unwinding by powerwashing some more in GTA," they wrote. But if we're scoring Jason's efforts? "7.8/10, too much water."

So there you go! The experts have spoken, and I'd call it a success for Rockstar's inaugural attempt at powerwashing, despite a handful of 'must try harders'. An unexpectedly generous response indeed! And if you're curious how FuturLab does it, look no further than last year's PowerWash Simulator 2. And for help with powerwashing in GTA 6, we've got a guide.

The Nathan Fielder/Lance Oppenheim co-directed hit documentary You Can See Everything, which has done huge box office numbers on the 2026 movie schedule, does a very deep dive into Elizabeth Holmes after Theranos. Now, everyone from former employees to psychologists is weighing in on Holmes both before and after her fraud convictions led to a long prison sentence that she is currently serving in Texas. Recently, one of Holmes’ assistants, Aria Marinelli, from the early days of Theranos, appeared on the Assistants vs. Agents podcast and spoke about a few red flags she saw in her short time working for the disgraced CEO.

Marinelli worked for Holmes at Theranos in 2009, which lands right in the middle of the company’s history, which was founded in 2003 and collapsed in 2016 before going completely out of business in 2018. Holmes went to prison in 2023. Marinelli wasn’t at the company long, by the sound of things, but did work directly for Holmes in her time with the Silicon Valley startup that promised big things with what we now know was a completely fraudulent blood-testing machine (a machine Marinelli says she never even laid eyes on until seeing You Can See Everything).

In the interview, she highlights a few things that made her question whether she wanted to be part of the company and if what they were doing was legitimate. According to Marinelli, the suspicions started even before she accepted the job, as she explained:

I went and looked through old emails just to see if I was remembering correctly, and it turns out I was. So this is [an email to] a mentor of mine. I said: ‘It's looking like I have to get Theranos an answer tomorrow regarding their offer. It expires at COB, and they've already extended it once. I'm very hesitant to accept because the work and the work environment are really not my ideal next step. Something about it doesn't sit right, I guess.’

She went on to explain that pretty early on, there was never a lot of talk about what the company was trying to do with the machine. In typical Silicon Valley style, according to Marinelli, most of the talk was about stock shares, IPOs, and how much money they could all make. That was something else that didn’t sit right with her.

Not only did Marinelli never see the now-infamous device, but she never saw a blood testing lab at all and was worried that despite famous names on the board of directors, there seemed to be no one with medical knowledge. That also raised concerns for her, as she explained:

The biggest thing was that there was no lab. So I had noticed that there were no doctors on the board, and that's, again, been talked about ad nauseam, but I was willing to dismiss that as maybe they were just getting started, right? And I remember just being told, ‘Oh, it's off-site,’ but I never saw anybody in that time frame that was working in a lab or that was from that lab.

The final straw for Marinelli was when she was tasked with tracking down one of the company’s machines from the Army, which was supposedly testing it. Through multiple emails and phone calls, she seemed to be a wild goose chase, with everyone pointing to other people, and no one knowing where the device actually was. Marinelli told host Warner Bailey:

Everyone [at Theranos] is very secretive, very, you know, shielded in how they're speaking about this thing. I doubt they would just ship it off to someone and not have them have a concerted program around testing it.  So that, to me, was kind of the last flag that I was willing to put up with.

Marinelli also gave her honest impression of Holmes, and it wasn’t all negative, but she did mention that she thought The Dropout, the series starring Amanda Seyfried that can be seen with a Hulu subscription, is a fair portrayal of Holmes as Marinelli knew her. She also praised You Can See Everything and seems to have real sympathy for Holmes, saying, “everyone has to lie at that level.”

One of the many interesting and brilliant things about You Can See Everything is that everyone sees something different in it, including the people who worked for Holmes and Theranos, and I don’t think this is the last time we’ll hear from people who worked with her and knew her. Especially as this movie continues to get Oscar buzz and will continue to be in the cultural zeitgeist for some time.

#3619. GTA 6 causes surge in UK physical game sales, despite there being no disc in the box

Grand Theft Auto 6 has had a huge effect on physical game sales in the UK, despite not actually containing a disc in the box.

NielsenIQ data shows that GTA 6 drove boxed software sales up an enormous 409 percent for the launch period ending 21st November, compared to the previous week, resulting in the biggest week for UK physical game sales since Christmas 2018.

GTA 6 alone accounted for £32m of the total £43m boxed software sales, apparently - around 74 percent, with 88 percent of its sales generated on day-one. But it's not a champion or record-breaker in this regard. In fact, GTA 6 places 17th in the all-time table of first-week boxed revenue, which is refreshingly humbling given the money-making records it's been breaking elsewhere. This is to do with the overwhelming shift towards buying games digitally, of course.

Nevertheless, Rockstar is well represented in the all-time list (which stretches back to 1995), because it's none other than GTA 5 that sits at the top, and GTA 4 at 11th.

But the GTA 6 effect is that of a rising tide, with console hardware sales rising 38 percent, to their highest level since 2025. Specifically, PS5 sales rose 46 percent and Xbox Series sales jumped a considerable 75 percent. And it's been a similar result in the US, where PS5 and Xbox Series sales have more than doubled.

Gaming accessory sales also got a boost, with PS5 controller sales up 355 percent, gaming headset sales up 94 percent, and - more nichely - gaming chair sales up 32 percent, which is apparently in line with the 40 percent increase they experienced around GTA 5.

"While the physical games market looks very different today compared with previous blockbuster launches, GTA 6 has still made a huge impact," said NielsenIQ's Dorian Bloch. "Back in 2008, boxed software accounted for half of all games retail revenue for the combined sectors of software, hardware, and gaming accessories, compared with 15 percent so far in 2026. This is a reflection of the market increasingly shifting towards digital downloads."

It's against this backdrop, of course, that Sony made its hugely controversial decision to wind down production of PlayStation game discs starting January 2028. This has led to boycotts and backlash and much angry sentiment towards the company, but Grand Theft Auto 6's enormous digital success is likely to be a hard example to ignore.

#3618. Nioh and Ninja Gaiden studio is using AI for QA, but argues "that a game becomes fun when crafted by human hands"

Team Ninja (Nioh, Ninja Gaiden) is the latest game development studio to implement AI into some of its workflow, but producer Kohei Shibata still believes that fun games need to be "crafted by human hands."

The producer best known for the tough-as-nails Nioh trilogy and Wo Long: Fallen Dynasty spoke about the controversial tech during South Korea's GCON 2026, in an interview with INVEN Global. "Currently, we utilize AI in QA and various verification tasks to streamline certain workflows," Shibata explained.

He went on to argue that if AI can "shorten task times," then developers can spend more hours "elevating the game's overall quality" in other ways. "In that sense, using AI is beneficial." Team Ninja isn't fully on board with enforcing the tech elsewhere, though: "Since it's still a new technology, we are continuously evaluating the most appropriate ways to implement it. I imagine other game companies are facing similar questions." (Good spot, Kotaku.)

"What matters fundamentally is that a game becomes fun when crafted by human hands. Repetitive, simple tasks that anyone must perform can be streamlined using technology. But ultimately, deciding how to craft the game and what makes it enjoyable must be done by humans. Using AI itself should never become the goal. I believe the principle that humans must think for themselves and finish the game will remain unchanged in the future," Shibata continued.

Generative AI's use in game development is still a hotly debated topic among both players and the people making games, but it's been prevalent nonetheless. A recent report estimated that around 40 percent of game developers were using AI in some fashion, even if lots of them also agreed the tech was harmful. Bigger publishers like Ubisoft and Epic Games are more aggressively pursuing an AI-first future, too.

Team Ninja seems to be settling into a middle ground, at least, according to Shibata's statement. Speaking on the studio's approach to difficult games, he said that a player's failure should never be the game's fault. Dying in a game like Ninja Gaiden or Nioh should always be the result of human error, otherwise death "causes frustration." Finding that perfect, often bloody sweet spot is something only humans can do.

#3616. Summer House’s Paige DeSorbo Posts 1st Video With Boyfriend Joe D'Amelio

Paige DeSorbo has gone social media official with boyfriend, Joe D’Amelio, by referencing one of the most famous mob movies of all-time.

The Summer House alum, 34, debuted D’Amelio, 37, via her TikTok and Instagram Stories on Wednesday, November 25, posting a fun clip of her loved ones making homemade pizza.

As the camera panned across the people taking part in the pizza party, D’Amelio was one of the figures introduced in the sweet clip as part of her crew.

For the post’s accompanying audio, DeSorbo used a clip of a voiceover taken from Martin Scorsese‘s classic 1990 film Goodfellas, where lead character Henry Hill (played by late actor Ray Liotta) introduces his crew.

“There was Jimmy, and Tommy, and me. And there was Anthony Stabile, Frankie Carbone,” Liotta can be heard saying as Hill during the famous quote. “And then there was Mo Black’s brother, Fat Andy and his guys, Frankie the Wop and Freddy No Nose. And then there was Pete the Killer, who was Sally Balls’ brother. Then you had Nickey Eyes and Mikey Franzese.”

Us confirmed in July 2025 that DeSorbo had moved on following her 2024 split from Southern Charm star Craig Conover and was “quietly dating” D’Amelio, a sports marketing executive.

“Things between them are going really well,” a source told Us at the time. “It took a few months for Paige to warm up to being in another relationship again, but she moved on after Craig and is genuinely happy.”

The pair have kept relatively tight-lipped about their budding romance and have kept their private life together mostly off social media until now.

Speaking exclusively to Us in February, DeSorbo confirmed that her relationship with D’Amelio was still going strong.

“We’re exclusive,” DeSorbo said at the time. “I’m in my 30s, so it’s not like I’m out every single weekend going out on multiple dates like I would have been in my 20s.”

The former reality star also described their connection as “really fun” and “very relaxing.”

Although she is no stranger to the public eye thanks to her past involvement with Summer House from 2019 to 2025 and previously being part of a public relationship, DeSorbo explained she was opting for a different approach this time around.

“It was such a balancing act,” she recalled to Us at the time. “I feel like when I was on reality TV — I started when I was 25 — it feels very, like, that was my 20s. Obviously, I’m in charge of my own decisions and stuff [now]. So it’s nice to be able to decide what I share and what I don’t [with] personal stuff.”

DeSorbo announced her departure from Summer House in 2025, months after confirming on her “Giggly Squad” podcast that she and Conover had split.

“Craig and I have decided to no longer be together. I love him, I think he loves me. I think we will remain friends,” she said in December 2024. “No one did anything. It wasn’t a bad thing. I think we both were just being really mature and saying what we want and what we didn’t want, and I think that’s extremely powerful to be able to voice how you’re feeling in real time and what you want for your future.”

#3615. The Witcher 3's new patch adds 40 cross-platform mods, fixes plenty of game-breaking bugs and "various lighting issues"

"The Path never sleeps, and the work is never done."

Developer CD Projekt Red has rolled out a new patch for The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt - Remastered on all platforms, which squashes dozens of bugs and adds 40 cross-platform mods with "more on the way."

"Two things are certain in a witcher's life: the Path never sleeps, and the work is never done," the studio wrote in its latest exhaustive list of patch notes for the decade-old game.

Patch 5.02's handiest changes come from those aforementioned bug fixes, many of which once caused the game to crash entirely or simply not work as intended. One such bug caused "time to go backwards indefinitely." Another turned Geralt bald. Opening the game with outdated mods could also result in a crash on PC. All of those, plus plenty more, have been fixed.

When The Witcher 3 Remastered first dropped, many players also took issue with the game's updated and sometimes "lifeless" lighting. Previous CDPR patches already targeted the lighting changes in question, but this newest patch continues to fix "various lighting issues across multiple locations and cutscenes."

The studio specifically names "overly bright or dark areas" and "inconsistent lighting transitions and flickering."

The Witcher 3's free remastered upgrade also gave all console owners access to mod support, though not all pre-existing PC mods were available to download for console folks. This patch is expanding the selection somewhat with 40 new cross-platform mods, including glowy eyes for Geralt and a new monster hunt - and on social media, the studio promised "more on the way."

CD Projekt Red is still hard at work on two big upcoming sequels, The Witcher 4 and Cyberpunk 2. Speaking on the former in a recent earnings call, joint-CEO Michal Nowakowski said we can expect a similar leap between The Witcher 3 and The Witcher 4 as we've just seen from GTA 5 to GTA 6.

I'm a hardcore reality TV fan, and this year is my first time watching a full season of The Great British Baking Show with my Netflix subscription. While longtime fans have been criticizing its twists or coming after the way Nigella Lawson eats, I've had a total blast watching the heartwarming competition series. Although I will say I totally called out a problem from Day 1 that ended up having a big impact on the semifinals episode.

Following Connie's truly heartbreaking elimination, the semifinal episode of Bake Off featured the top four contestants creating Patisseries. There was just one big problem: the heat wave in the U.K. was making it especially hot in the iconic tent. Unfortunately that threw a wrench into the baker's plans, especially when they needed the time to cool their bakes. I thought this was going to be a big problem over the course of the season, and I feel totally vindicated after watching the semifinal episode of the season.

The struggle of cooling bakes has been a recurring theme throughout this season of Bake Off, and it had major implications during Patisserie week. This was especially true for the technical challenge, where contestants needed to create judge Paul Hollywood's Gateau Concorde in 21⁄2 hours. Inside the tent was reportedly a whopping 94 degrees, and a number of the bakes suffered as a result.

Unfortunately, Gabe struggled quite a bit during the semifinals, partially thanks to the heat and his bakes not being able to properly cool. He ended up being eliminated before the finals, but he wasn't the only one who had issues with the heat while trying to craft his patisseries. Frontrunner Tom's babas were also underproofed, so it was clear that the heat wave was affecting the whole cast. I can't imagine how it must have felt to be so hot while baking, especially because I also tend to overheat when experiencing anxiety.

There's just one episode for this season of The Great British Baking Show, so the pressure is on for the final there bakers to stick the landing and hopefully pull out a W. While fans across the pond already know who will take the prize, we here in the states will have to wait until Black Friday to stream the finale episode on Netflix. I'm especially curious to see if the U.K. heatwave from last summer continues to be a menace for the contestants during their final few bakes. Can't we get some better air conditioning in the Bake Off tent?

The Great British Baking Show releases new episodes of Netflix as part of the 2026 TV schedule. I've had a blast enjoying my first full season of the long-running competition series, and I'll definitely be back to watch the next season.

#3613. EA removes some live service fluff from Skate and ends seasonal structure "in favour of regular, agile content updates"

EA is ditching seasonal updates and shaving some of the live service fluff off Skate (for some reason stylised as skate.) going forward. Normally, such news would be cause for concern. Here, the publisher assured players the transition will lead to more regular updates since devs can now push out new features without waiting for the next season to roll around.

"EA and Full Circle are committed to keep driving skate. forward. Just as a reminder, we're still very much in Early Access," the studio wrote in a new blog post. "The game is still a work in progress, and we're using this valuable time to experiment, iterate, and figure out what works best for the long-term health of the game - especially when it comes to social features and progression. Ultimately, we want to build skate. in a way that lets us roll out fresh content much faster, even if it's not totally finished yet."

Skate's fifth and final season is coming to an end on 1st December, with Full Circle embracing a different model from there on out. "We are transitioning away from the traditional seasonal cadence in favor of regular, agile content updates," it explained.

Full Circle is also throwing out the skating sim's version of a seasonal battle pass (horribly named skate.Pass) by the end of the year, and will rethink how the game's progression system works: "We've said it many times: we have a long-term future vision for skate, and this is a key part of it. Update 0.33.1 will be our very first update in this post-season era."

The move away from rigid seasonal updates "gives the development team the freedom to launch features earlier in their lifecycle," the blog post continued. "This means we can deploy work-in-progress mechanics and gather your direct feedback to continuously shape and build upon San Vansterdam. We've started this with in-game testing of features such as Spot Battles, Block Parties, and Prox Chat before rolling it out officially, and we’re going to continue with this process."

Full Circle's live service rejig also means the in-game currency Tix is being retired, and some maps will no longer be locked behind paywalls. Skate still has real-money microtransactions and a cosmetics store, though it's nice to see some of the more aggressive live service bits being plucked out.

1. Check your motherboard's SSD sockets/ports first

2. Get the largest capacity SSD you can afford

3. Get yourself a Gen4 (PCIe 4.0) NVMe SSD

4. DRAM-less SSDs are perfectly fine for gaming

5. Check your motherboard to see if you need an SSD with a pre-fitted heatsink

Black Friday officially starts on Friday, November 27, but the deals tend to start rolling in a few days before that. Black Friday doesn't end until November 30, when we roll into even more online deals through Cyber Monday.

It's easy to get carried away at this time of year, but if you know how much you want to spend and what sort of SSD you're after, you'll be in good stead.

Capacity is a good starting point. At the moment, we're looking at some excellent 1 TB, 2 TB and 4 TB offers. A 512 GB SSD could still afford you a lot of speedy storage for a boot drive, with enough space for a handful of games, depending on the size, but this capacity is very slim nowadays. With memory supply crisis prices though, 512 GB isn't really the best value proposition anymore though.

Then think about the interface. Chances are, if you've been rocking a PC for the last five years, you'll have an M.2 slot in your motherboard with NVMe support. However, it's worth digging into the specifics of your motherboard to ensure it can support booting from such drives as not all can. Check out the manufacturer's pages and maybe forums too.

It's also worth thinking about which version of the PCIe interface your storage slots operate on. On the AMD side, from the Ryzen 3000-series and up you should expect to have PCIe 4.0 slots on your motherboard, and from Intel's 11th-Gen Rocket Lake chips the same should be true. PCIe 4.0 drives are the more mainstream option today, which are widely supported. The faster PCIe 5.0 standard is pretty pricey and not necessarily worth it for gamers.

There are some things to look out for, however. Some budget PCIe 3.0 drives only operate at x2 speed, which means they're half as fast as the standard x4 NVMe SSDs. These are pretty rare nowadays but it's worth double checking. It's also worth ensuring your M.2 SSD is an NVMe drive. There are some M.2 SSDs that still operate over the SATA interface and can only reach a maximum theoretical speed of 600 MB/s, while even a PCIe 4.0 drive can hit over 7,000 MB/s.

There are always reasons to hold off on making a new purchase whenever you are thinking about making one. Whether it's the potential for a new generation of techie goodness on the horizon—either cutting prices on existing models or delivering tangible higher performance—or because there might be an imminent sale looming.

When picking out SSD deals we take all of this into consideration, and where we think prices on something might significantly drop on the big day itself we simply won't recommend it. But all of the products here we either believe won't significantly drop much further in terms of their pricing, or are just good deals that we wouldn't hesitate recommending if you wanted to make a purchase today.

#3611. Team Ninja Is Using AI For Quality Assurance, But Insists Creative Choices ‘Must Be Done By Humans’

Team Ninja is known, in part, for developing difficult games, but producers Kohei Shibata and Masakazu Hirayama emphasized during an interview with INVEN Global at GCON 2026 in South Korea that thereâs a key difference between difficult and unfair. The pair also spoke about how the Koei Tecmo subsidiary approaches the use of AI in games development, and an awkward compromise between implementing the technology for repetitive QA tasks, while arguing that “what matters fundamentally is that a game becomes fun when crafted by human hands.”

Shibata and Hirayama are best known for their work as producers on the Nioh and Wo Long series respectively, two games that take the combat-driven difficulty of the iconic Ninja Gaiden franchise and transpose it onto the world of samurai and Chinese mythology. Before the topic of AI arose, the two discussed the crucial role of player interaction and movement in their games, beginning with the similarities between all three franchises and most notably their swordplay and the focus on timing your attacks and reading an opponentâs next move. According to both, this process of requiring a player to learn an enemyâs next move and counter is key to straddling the line between challenging and frustrating play.

âI consider Nioh to be samurai action,â explained Shibata. âSamurai combat involves stillness and movement. You stand firmly grounded, observing the opponent’s moves, and deliver a sharp strike the instant an opening appears.â Meanwhile, for Hirayama on Wo Long, that game was defined by âaggressive Chinese martial arts action,â where âattack and defense flow together seamlesslyâ and where âaggressively attacking is important, but defense must also lead directly into the next attack.â

The two go on to argue that it’s important to make a game that is polished in a way that reduces friction between a player’s action and consequence. If a person fails, it must be their fault, not the game’s. âI believe [the core essence of action games is] control responsiveness,â Shibata explained. âWhen a player presses a button, the character must move exactly as they intended. If you press a button and the character doesn’t react properly, it causes frustration. Conversely, if a slight input causes an exaggerated movement, it feels awkward. Therefore, responsiveness to input must be simple and intuitive, and the movement must be communicated rapidly.â

We have seen numerous studios speak out in recent times about where they will and wonât use AI. While some Japanese developers are embracing the technology, others are more cautious, either avoiding it entirely or insisting they only use the technology for optimizing their development framework while leaving creative choices to humans. The latter is the direction being taken by Capcom with its next generation of RE Engine, and appears to also be the choice being made by Team Ninja, who are already using AI for QA purposes.

As Shibata explained, âCurrently, we utilize AI in QA and various verification tasks to streamline certain workflows. If we can use AI to shorten task times, we can dedicate that saved time toward elevating the game’s overall quality. In that sense, using AI is beneficial. However, since it is still a new technology, we are continuously evaluating the most appropriate ways to implement it. I imagine other game companies are facing similar questions.” He continued,

What matters fundamentally is that a game becomes fun when crafted by human hands. Repetitive, simple tasks that anyone must perform can be streamlined using technology. But ultimately, deciding how to craft the game and what makes it enjoyable must be done by humans. Using AI itself should never become the goal. I believe the principle that humans must think for themselves and finish the game will remain unchanged in the future.

Where, if anywhere, is an acceptable use of AI is a topic that remains up for debate, but it appears many developers are settling into a space where it is used to handle repetitive tasks. The use of AI in QA actually predates the modern conversations of generative AI, and doesnât necessarily rely on the tech: Sony, for instance, has been experimenting with AI for many years to test games. Whether this is something audiences are willing to tolerate, or indeed is something that will further threaten jobs in the games industry, remains to be seen.

For months, some fan favorites and newcomers alike at Warner Bros., New Line, Weta and even Hobbiton have been prepping for a brand new Lord of the Rings movie. Lips have been pretty tightly sealed about the new Hunt for Gollum project beyond the fact it’s set during the time shortly before the Fellowship of the Ring and will feature Andy Serkis both as director and Gollum himself. Returning cast members include Ian McKellen, Lee Pace and Elijah Wood stepping back into those Hobbit feet. Oh, and Jamie Dornan and Leo Woodall will provide some additional eye candy. (And good acting too, credit where credit is due!)

It’s hard to believe The Lord of The Rings: The Hunt For Gollum has already wrapped. The movie picked up principle photography in July of this year, and has been quietly chugging along for months, but it still feels like yesterday it was getting off the ground. This morning, Andy Serkis and co. revealed the movie has wrapped in a new post that has me champing at the bit to see what’s next.

The news comes just a few weeks after Jamie Dornan admitted he’d wrapped his own portion of the movie. (There may have been some crying involved.) For his part, Andy Serkis has shared his return in the mo-cap suit, and now we've gotten a taste at Gollum's return in this funny wrap video.

To note, I’m not the only one impressed by Serkis donning the mo-cap suit at 62, either.

Warner Bros. revealed the new franchise film will be returning to the Shire back in September, a fact I can also confirm thanks to a lovely visit to the set of the movie and Hobbiton, courtesy of the studio. The movie shot for several days on location in the real-life version of the Shire on the Alexander Farm before heading to the soundstage in New Zealand, and the end result should be nothing short of epic, but that will also mean there’s plenty to do in post ahead. The movie itself isn’t scheduled to hit theaters for over a year, but I’ll take any tidbit I can get in the meantime.

It’s been a great holiday season for Lord of the Rings fans already. Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power dropped its final two episodes for Season 3 this week, and Season 4 was announced! Now, we know the upcoming 2027 movie release is ready to go into post-production. It's a big week, but December 17th, 2027 couldn’t come soon enough.

The Saudi Arabian investment group is struggling to turn a profit from its investment in renowned Japanese developer SNK, as the 48-year-old company faces heavy losses following lower than expected sales. However, it might have have found a new medium through which to claw back its cash: the movies. After all, SNK’s series likeÂ Fatal Fury, The King of Fighters and Metal Slug still hold cultural capital. Amidst Saudi Arabiaâs many other investments is new film studio The Arena, which has just announced Metal Slug as the latest property from the game studio to be in the works for a movie adaptation.

First reported by Variety, the studio announced that the adaptation of the side-scrolling military action platformer is going ahead, withÂ I Love My Dad director James Morosini attached to the project. An initial plot loosely based on the already thin narrative of theÂ Metal Slug series has also been revealed, centered on a misfit quartet of army recruits known as Marco Rossi, Tarma Roving, Eri Kasamoto and Fio Germi, as they stand up to General Morden to save the world from evil. Which seems about as coherent as a movie based on a game where soldiers fight aliens, yetis and zombies can get.

The Arena, originally revealed last year as Arena SNK Studios, is headed up by Erik Feig, a veteran producer who helped bring the likes of Twilight and La La Land to the screen. It was formed with backing from Saudi Arabiaâs Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, and so far all of its projects bar one have been licensed from the SNK library. Currently in production is a webtoon called The Art of Fighting, and a TV series and movie based on Fatal Fury. It’s also working on a movie tied to Samurai Spirits, another SNK property. Their only non-SNK project is adapting a yet-to-be-released novel known as Kill Current.

Since its unveiling, the Arena’s only tangible output has been selling SNK fashion merchandise and running an Instagram account that seems to post about almost anything except its actual movies. Still, perhaps these movies and the occasional clothing merchandising drop are where investors hope to make back their money on buying SNK. Metal Slug at least has a concept lending itself to a more typical action blockbuster, but the question remains, with most of the studioâs IP resonating more with older audiences, can they turn these SNK IPs into something with mass appeal?
